MINOR: Module-level `os.environ.setdefault("PF_HIL_TOKEN", ...)` mutates process-global state at import time, coupling this wrapper to import order within a shared pytest session (any test asserting token-absent startup behavior in the same process becomes order-dependent).

`setdefault` never overrides a `PF_HIL_TOKEN` already present in the ambient environment (dev shell/CI), so tests may exercise real token material instead of the deterministic fixture value, breaking test determinism.
Import-time side effect is undocumented (no comment on why the wrapper must inject the token); a fixture/`monkeypatch`-scoped setup would keep the mutation bounded and self-describing.
NIT: Hardcoded `"hil-tok"` literal inline; a named constant would make intent and any future rotation obvious.
SUMMARY: Delta is test-only env bootstrap for the wrapper; no shipped-code change, contract change, or language-rule violation, so nothing rises to BLOCKER/MAJOR.
Top risks are test isolation (global env mutation, import-order coupling) and silent absorption of a real ambient token; both are hardening-level for this delta.
